methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $700M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised $700M+ in total capital, including a 2024 recapitalization led by Niobrara Capital and Prysm Capital. The Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though narrow-stage peer multiples are insufficient for reliable triangulation.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised of $700M as a proxy for recent valuation and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $840M. This method is applicable given Polar's positioning within the Growth cohort. Peer-median comparison cannot be applied due to insufficient same- or adjacent-stage datapoints within the Chips & Semiconductors universe (only 1 adjacent-stage peer identified). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples is not feasible; while the three public semiconductor comparables trade at a median 21.4x price-to-sales, Polar's revenue is not disclosed, preventing meaningful application.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $714M to $966M, with a median of $840M. This range reflects limited methodological coverage driven by data constraints inherent to private semiconductor companies. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed revenue (blocking public multiple approaches) and the sparse private peer set at identical stage. Any valuation within this band should be stress-tested against Polar's actual revenue run-rate and capital efficiency relative to disclosed peers.
